$comment: One declaration of PR composition inputs (HA#171, HA#351). Reader ids, templates, titles, families and defaults live in contracts/pr-sections.json. Readers resolve a per-run requirements array; the checked default is process.canon. Gate and changelog path sets remain solely here. scripts/pr_composition_check.sh refuses drift and copied path sets. The gateDerive rows include zheref/nen under HA#334; moving those inputs into a declared Nen home remains owed, as docs/PROCESS.md records.

bodyRequirements.$comment: Derived from the catalogue, not a universal template. Runtime resolution uses the target kind, issue jobs and Mukai facts. This checked array is the process.canon default with a policy hit.

gateDerive.$comment: nen gate derive --policy-paths / --process-paths, keyed by the canon repository (owner/name) whose own canon the sets are. A consumer repository is G2 by role and the verb is not run (docs/WORKFLOW.md section Gate derivation, step 1); a canon repository with no row here has no declared sets, which the run states and asks for (docs/WORKFLOW.md section 4, Ask, set up, continue) and never improvises. Each value is passed comma-joined, in the order written. Both nen/ and schemas/ stay listed: a prefix is taken literally, and an un-migrated target still edits a real schemas/*.json. contracts/ and templates/ are in zheref/hatsu's process set so this declaration, the requirements array and the template derive G4 as WORKFLOW.md did when it held the sets -- confirmed by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-10-13 (docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-10-13; zheref/hatsu#171).

zheref/nen.$comment: zheref/hatsu#334. THE MAINTAINER'S RULING OF 2026-10-20, asked through the picker (docs/ROSTER.md section Rulings of 2026-10-20 -- zheref/nen's gate path sets): every top-level entry of nen's tracked tree derives G4 except LICENSE and .gitignore. nen is canon by role (nen/repos.json maintained_tools; `nen repo classify --target zheref/nen` answers role canon, gate G4), and its product is the process in the words of the ROSTER ruling of 2026-09-18: prose, scripts and deterministic jobs together. Each member is a top-level entry of nen's tracked tree at v0.23.0 (1d2fb6f) or at nen main on 2026-10-20, which adds changelog.d/; bunfig.toml and .npmrc are listed as literal entries though absent from both, since either would change how the binary is built or how its dependencies resolve. policyPaths: nen/ is nen's own policy (gates.json, workflow.json, labels.json, repos.json, contract.json); schemas/ is absent there and kept for the literal-prefix reason above. processPaths is the rest: src/ is the binary every consumer runs; bootstrap/ is the script every consumer fetches at a pinned ref; profiles/ is the stack reference pack shu detect proposes from; templates/ is what scaffold writes into other repositories; docs/ is the verb spec and the stack catalogue; README.md is the documented verb surface; CHANGELOG.md and changelog.d/ carry the consumer notes that move the compatible-minor floor; tests/ and the tool configs (tsconfig.json, eslint.config.js, vitest.config.ts, bunfig.toml) decide what the shipped binary is and how it is verified; package.json, bun.lock and .npmrc are the dependencies built into it; .gitattributes decides how its files are checked out and diffed; .github/ is whole, not only .github/workflows/, because its workflows build and gate the published release assets and any file added beside them (a dependabot.yml, say) would change what goes into them. Only LICENSE and .gitignore derive G2, alone or together. FALL-THROUGH, stated: a top-level entry nen adds later that neither set lists derives G2 until this row moves, so a tree-freshness check at repin is owed -- list nen's tree at the pinned tag and fail when a top-level entry is in neither set nor the explicit G2 list (docs/PROCESS.md section Residue and owned dependencies; not yet filed). This is the ruling for zheref/nen only: zheref/hatsu's own row above is unchanged, so a diff of only its README.md or CHANGELOG.md still derives G2 there. OWNERSHIP: these are another canon repository's sets, held by Hatsu until nen has a declared home of its own that nen gate derive reads; that home is owed to nen, not yet filed. The representative changes and their expected gates are scripts/pr_composition_check_fixture.sh's zheref/nen cases, derived by nen gate derive itself.

changelogFragment.$comment: nen changelog fragment-required --spec-paths (comma-joined) --fragment-dir --head-changelog, every target; --head-changelog resolves against --repo. A pull request that changes a specPaths path owes a fragment under fragmentDir (CONTRIBUTING.md, Changelog fragments) and reads fragment-present with no opt-out. directSection is the one case that does not: a pull request that writes its own section into headChangelog, as futon's integration PR does (docs/ROSTER.md, Rulings of 2026-09-30 -- En never merges: the terminus carries the CHANGELOG). Its body carries `optOut` verbatim, and only when its own diff changes headChangelog. UNENFORCED BY NEN: the verb honours the phrase anywhere -- over any diff, inside an HTML comment or a code fence -- so a body carrying it over any other diff passes; a Hatsu-side raw-body check is owed, and so is the nen half, the verb honouring the phrase only in the body's own prose (not yet filed).

directSection.when: the pull request's own changed files include headChangelog
directSection.optOut: no CHANGELOG entry: this pull request writes its own CHANGELOG.md section (contracts/pr-composition.json, changelogFragment.directSection)
